title: Minimizing the stabbing number of matchings, trees, and triangulations
contribution: SODA 2004 version: NP-hardness of minimum stabbing problems by one proof technique, plus a cut-based IP whose LP gives polynomial-time lower bounds and a provably heavy fractional edge towards iterated rounding, solving instances with several hundred points (abstract).
problem_entry: The complexity of minimum-stabbing-number perfect matchings, spanning trees and triangulations was a long-standing open question, one of the original 30 problems of the Demaine-Mitchell-O'Rourke list (abstract).
key_idea: Hardness by a general proof technique, then a cut-based IP for matchings and spanning trees whose LP relaxation yields polynomial-time lower bounds and an optimal fractional solution with an edge of at least constant weight (abstract). The v1 (SODA) abstract states NP-completeness and says this 'suggests' constant-factor approximations (arXiv v1 abstract page). The abstracts.json text is the final arXiv (DCG, card D001) abstract, identical to DataCite's record.
assumptions: Point sets in the plane; axis-parallel or general stabbing lines; perfect matchings, spanning trees, triangulations (abstract).
proof_devices: general proof technique for NP-hardness of minimum stabbing problems, implying lower bounds on approximability (abstract)
cut-based IP formulation for matchings and spanning trees; LP relaxation gives lower bounds in polynomial time (abstract)
an optimal fractional solution always contains an edge of at least constant weight, the step towards iterated rounding (abstract)
experiments: Problems with up to several hundred points solved optimally or near-optimally (abstract); no test set, solver or times in the abstract. v1 has 2 tables (arXiv comment) while the journal text omits the details (card D001, D5), so the computations are probably in this version (inferred).
positioning: Answers an open question from the Demaine-Mitchell-O'Rourke list of open problems in computational geometry (abstract).
writing: Negative answer stated first, then 'On the positive side'; the approximation framed as 'a crucial step towards' (abstract).
limits_future: The constant-factor approximation is not yet obtained, only a step towards it (abstract).

method_links.note: Step 6: the approximation is claimed only as 'a crucial step towards' a constant-factor guarantee; v1 said the heavy edge 'suggests' one.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Existing candidate (D001): polynomial-time LP lower bounds and a provably heavy fractional edge for iterated rounding.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: first exact IP in a theory-dominated area
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Existing candidate (D001): a cut-based IP after the hardness result, solving instances with several hundred points optimally or near-optimally.

transferable: After a hardness proof, write one cut-based IP whose LP relaxation gives polynomial-time lower bounds, whose optimal fractional solutions provably contain a heavy variable for iterated rounding, and which also solves instances of realistic size exactly (abstract).

quotes.text: The (axis-parallel) stabbing number of a given set of line segments is the maximum number of segments that can be intersected by any one (axis-parallel) line.
in fact, it is one of the original 30 outstanding open problems in computational geometry on the list by Demaine, Mitchell, and O'Rourke

title: Improved Column Generation for Highly Degenerate Master Problems
contribution: Improved column generation reduces a degenerate master to the rows of its non-degenerate basic variables, prices compatible columns (or adds incompatible ones with a dynamic update) and strictly improves the objective each time, with IPS and DCA as special cases (abstract).
problem_entry: Column generation suffers from degeneracy, the tailing-off effect; the entry is a transfer of recent advances against degeneracy in the primal simplex method (abstract).
key_idea: Reduce the master's rows to the number of non-degenerate basic variables (smaller basis, faster re-optimization); pricing generates columns compatible with the row reduction if possible, otherwise incompatible columns are added and the reduction is updated dynamically (abstract).
assumptions: Linear programs with a huge number of variables solved by column generation; degenerate restricted master solutions (abstract).
proof_devices: row reduction of the restricted master to its non-degenerate basic variables (abstract)
pricing restricted to columns compatible with the row reduction, with incompatible columns and a dynamic update as fallback (abstract)
strict improvement of the objective in either case (abstract)
experiments: None of its own in the abstract; it cites recent experiments with IPS and DCA on highly degenerate LPs (abstract).
positioning: Inspired by the primal simplex literature on degeneracy; the improved primal simplex method and dynamic constraints aggregation are its two special cases (abstract).
writing: Unconditional claims ('We show that, in either case, a strict improvement ... occurs'; 'larger impact ... than the column-reduction') that the 2013 revision S031 hedges (abstract; S031 p. 1).
limits_future: Extensions and some implementation issues discussed (abstract).

method_links.note: Steps 1-2: starts from the tailing-off effect and puts two published remedies, IPS and DCA, under one method (co-authored, third author).

Step 6 across versions: the revision S031 drops 'Improved' and 'Highly' from the title, turns 'takes advantage' into 'may take advantage', makes the strict improvement conditional on a negative weighted combination of reduced costs, and drops the comparison with column reduction.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: turn the complicating feature into an advantage
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Existing candidate (S031): an ICG method 'that takes advantage of degenerate solutions'.

transferable: When the restricted master is degenerate, keep only the rows of its non-degenerate basic variables, price columns compatible with that row set, and when none exists add incompatible columns and update the row set, so that every iteration strictly improves the objective (abstract).

Before a working paper becomes a journal paper, rewrite each unconditional statement of its abstract as the condition under which it holds, and drop comparisons the paper does not measure itself (abstract against S031 p. 1).
coauthors: J. Desrosiers, J. B. Gauthier (Lübbecke third)

quotes.text: We show that, in either case, a strict improvement in the objective function value occurs.
Two special cases of ICG are the improved primal simplex method and the dynamic constraints aggregation.

title: Reform der Bundestagswahlkreise
contribution: For the Federal Election Commissioner, optimization-based Bundestag district divisions for 250, 200 and 125 districts with all legal criteria kept, showing that the district number matters and recommending 248 and 145 (abstract).
problem_entry: The electoral-law debate includes reducing the number of districts; on behalf of the Federal Election Commissioner the authors computed divisions for 250, 200 and 125 districts (abstract).
key_idea: All legal criteria strictly kept and the legal apportionment principles met as well as possible, nothing else added and no legally possible division excluded in advance (abstract); read as hard constraints plus a scored objective as in S080 p. 4 (inferred).
assumptions: German Bundestag districting under the legal criteria and apportionment principles; one- and two-person districts (abstract).
experiments: Three scenarios and an interactive online map of all optimization-based divisions (abstract); no solver, run times or optimality figures in the abstract.
writing: The English abstract carries over the 2018 report's opening summary: 'sichert dabei Neutralität und Transparenz' (S080 p. 1) becomes 'guarantees objectivity and transparency' (abstract).
limits_future: A careless choice of the number of districts can have considerable consequences, up to numerical inadmissibility (abstract); this answers the question S080 left open, which number of districts fits best (S080 p. 2).

method_links.note: Checkpoint, abstract level: 'guarantees objectivity and transparency' and principles 'fulfilled in the best possible way' stand without optimality evidence, while the 2018 report proved optimality only for a few states or Regierungsbezirke; whether this article carries proofs is not read.
